questions.q: In "Who needs this, and who is your first user Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a half-page idea: who, what you will do, what success looks like in numbers.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing that is strong, one thing to fix.
Each learner reads their idea aloud (3 minutes).
Measure the result against your goal: cost per enquiry, conversion rate of the page, share of budget spent, enquiries per week.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Finish the task and fix the biggest problem found in the circle.
Each learner reads their idea aloud (3 minutes).

questions.q: In "Start the practice task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set up free analytics and a consent banner where rules require.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.

questions.q: In "Short modules Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Check numbers every 3 days: visits, enquiries, cost per enquiry.
Get a written note from one real user or expert where possible.
Analytics: count visits, actions and cost. Cost per enquiry = money spent divided by enquiries.

questions.q: In "Continue and log Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Channels: search, social, email, local listings. Choose the one or two where your buyer already is. Do not try all at once.
Pause the weakest advert and put its budget on the best one.
Pick one sample business and one goal with a number, such as 20 enquiries in 4 weeks.
Goal: 20 enquiries in 4 weeks for a local cleaning service. Budget cap 200.

questions.q: In "Finish and measure Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Talk to 3 to 5 possible users or experts. Ask: what do you do now, what is hard, what would make you trust a new service?
